chunks: SPI daisy-chaining explained. The question: How does daisy-chaining work?
A daisy chain connects SPI slaves one after another, like links in a chain. The master's data goes into the first chip.
Each chip passes its data on to the next, and the last chip sends it back to the master. All the chips share one clock and one chip select.
The whole chain acts like one long row of storage cells.
Imagine a line of people, each holding a card. On every beat of a drum, each person hands their card to the next person down the line.
To end up with a chosen card in every hand, you feed in the card for the farthest person first. Cards for nearer people go in later.
When a whistle blows, everyone keeps the card they hold. In SPI, that whistle is chip select going high.
SCLK and CS (top) are shared by all three devices; the data path is a single series loop: MOSI to Dev 1 to Dev 2 to Dev 3 to MISO.
Four wires from the master regardless of chain length.
Daisy chain: devices connected in series, so data passes through each one in turn. Shift register: a row of storage cells that moves every bit one place along on each clock tick.
Frame: one period with chip select low. Here it spans the whole chain. Latch: copying the collected bits into the part that drives the outputs.
It happens when chip select goes high. Chip select (CS): the shared wire that marks the frame.
Chain three chips, each holding 8 bits. You want them to end up with bytes A, B and C, in order from nearest the master to farthest. Pull CS low. Send C first, then B, then A.
That is 24 clock ticks, or 2. 4 microseconds at 10 megahertz. The first byte travels through two chips and settles in the last one.
Raise CS, and all three chips latch their bytes at the same moment. That is the whole idea.
"Daisy-chaining connects SPI slaves in series: MOSI goes into the first device, each device's output feeds the next input, and the last output returns on MISO, with SCLK and CS shared.
The chain behaves as one long shift register, so a frame is N words of clocks with CS low, the first word ends up in the last device, and the CS rising edge latches everything at once.
It saves pins and updates simultaneously, but every frame has to cover the whole chain and the parts must support it."
